channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [7] Superballistic flow of viscous electron fluid induced by edge magnetoplasmons in point contacts
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: K. W. West, Rui-Rui Du

Authors: Xinghao Wang, Wenfeng Zhang, Loren N. Pfeiffer, Kirk W. Baldwin, K. W. West, Rui-Rui Du

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Hydrodynamic electron transport is a key topic in modern correlated electron systems.

Tags: #transport #hydrodynamics #correlatedelectrons

Abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 06 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-73154-5 Superballistic transport is a known hydrodynamic effect where viscous electrons can move collectively. Here, the authors provide evidence of superballistic electron flow under microwave irradiation in point contacts induced by edge magnetoplasmons.
